title: Michael Burry closes his Nasdaq bets and shifts to value, but still plans an Nvidia short
body: Burry's moves are small in market terms, but they are closely watched by retail traders and can shape sentiment more than their size would suggest. Closing broad index shorts after a correction removes one well-known bearish voice from the tech trade, which may encourage dip-buyers in the near term. His $200 level for a fresh Nvidia short gives traders a reference point well above current prices, which suggests he expects any rebound to be overdone before he acts. Palantir remains the clearest single-stock target of his bearish view. --- investingLive Americas FX news wrap 25 Nov: It's a Wrap. S&P 500 and Nasdaq pare steep losses --- Michael Burry has taken his profits on the tech selloff and moved into cash and value stocks, but his doubts about Nvidia are only on hold until the price is right.

title: BofA sees S&P 500 at 7,800 by end-2027, a target that only takes it back to October
body: A low target from a big bank rarely moves the index on its own, but it adds weight to the view that the post-correction rebound will be harder work than the consensus near 8,500 assumes. The supply-and-demand argument is worth watching: if share issuance and IPOs keep rising while buybacks slow, mega-cap tech names that rely on steady buyback demand could lag the broader market. The sector picks point to banks and health care as relative winners if 2027 turns choppy, with consumer staples likely to lag. With Thanksgiving thinning out trade, outlooks like this are likely to shape positioning more than price action this week. --- Bank of America's 2027 target looks like an 8% gain but is really a round trip, and the bank expects even that to be bumpy. Summary: Bank of America's Savita Subramanian forecasts the S&P 500 at 7,800 by the end of 2027, about 8% above Tuesday's close The target would only return the index to its October record. It was first set as a 12-month target in September, when it implied about 2% upside Scenarios run from a bear case of 6,600 to a bull case of 8,500 The bank flags rising share issuance, fading buybacks, AI investment uncertainty and earnings risks Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley target 8,700, Deutsche Bank 9,000 and JPMorgan 8,200 BofA favors communication services, financials, health care and consumer discretionary, and is cautious on consumer staples Bank of America expects the S&P 500 to finish 2027 at 7,800.

title: AI's debt binge is becoming a bond market problem, South Africa's central bank warns
body: The SARB's warning adds an official voice to a concern that has mostly lived in credit markets until now, and it widens the debate from tech valuations to the cost of government borrowing. The most exposed markets are emerging-market bonds and currencies, which tend to suffer first when global investors cut risk. For equities, the concentration figure is the warning sign: when so much fund exposure sits in a handful of mega-cap names, a selloff in those stocks spreads quickly through portfolios worldwide. Long-end yields and credit spreads on heavily indebted AI borrowers are the gauges to watch alongside the chip stocks. --- Earlier: A junk-rated borrower with an AA-rated customer: CoreWeave's next loan leans on Meta --- The SARB has put into words what credit markets have been signalling all week: the AI boom's borrowing bill is now everyone's problem, governments included.

title: Moody's keeps Nvidia at Aa1 after Huang's return but flags key-person and governance risks
body: An unchanged rating removes one possible source of pressure on Nvidia's bonds, but it is unlikely to calm credit markets on its own, because the wider worry is leverage across the AI build-out rather than at Nvidia. For equity investors, the key-person warning is the part that sticks: the stock's reaction to Huang's exit and return showed that leadership risk is now part of its valuation. Any detail on the export-control rules Moody's referred to could matter more for Nvidia's shares than the rating itself. With US markets shut for Thanksgiving, the first proper reaction comes in Friday's shortened session. --- Earlier: A junk-rated borrower with an AA-rated customer: CoreWeave's next loan leans on Meta --- Moody's is comfortable with Nvidia's balance sheet, but less so with how much the company depends on one man and the scrutiny surrounding him.

title: Gold claws back $160 from a 14-month low, but one candle doesn't necessarily make a bottom
body: Reclaiming $3,500 gives gold bulls a floor to defend, but there's little sign of a confirmed turn until prices clear last week's high near $3,900. Silver followed the same path, bouncing from below $38 to above $41, which suggests broad short covering across precious metals rather than buying driven by gold alone. With US markets closed for Thanksgiving and Friday a short session, thin liquidity could exaggerate the next move in either direction. The bigger test comes with the Fed's December 9 decision, when the bank's guidance on further hikes is likely to matter more for real yields, and for gold, than the hike itself. --- Earlier: Gold bulls may have been waiting months for a chart like this --- Gold found buyers at its lowest level since September 2025, but bank forecasts ranging from $3,340 to $5,000 show how little agreement there is on where this correction ends.

title: U.S. Oil Rig Count Edges Higher as Baker Hughes Reports Modest Weekly Gain
body: The U.S. oil and gas sector showed a slight uptick in activity as the Baker Hughes oil rig count rose to 470, up from 469 previously, according to data updated on 25 November 2026. While the one-rig increase is modest, it signals that operators are at least maintaining, and potentially beginning to cautiously expand, drilling activity. The latest reading suggests that, for now, U.S. producers are not scaling back materially, keeping capacity broadly stable with a marginal upward bias. Market participants often monitor such changes week to week for early signs of shifts in supply that could influence price dynamics in the oil market. title: Brazil's FX Flows Swing Into the Red With $1.5B Outflow
body: Brazil's foreign exchange flows sharply reversed direction, moving from a net inflow to a significant net outflow, according to data updated on 25 November 2026. The latest reading shows FX flows at -$1.535 billion, compared with a previous level of +$1.293 billion. The negative figure indicates that, over the latest measured period, more foreign currency left Brazil than entered, marking a notable shift in cross-border capital movements. While the data release does not specify the underlying drivers, such a swing can reflect changes in investor sentiment, adjustments in trade flows, or repositioning in global financial markets. Market participants will be watching subsequent FX flow readings closely to determine whether this move is a temporary adjustment or the beginning of a more sustained trend in capital outflows from Brazil. title: U.S. Natural Gas Inventories Swing from Build to 24B Draw, Signaling Stronger Demand
body: U.S. natural gas storage levels have sharply reversed course, shifting from a 20B build to a 24B draw, according to data updated on 25 November 2026. The move marks a significant change in the weekly balance between supply and demand in the U.S. gas market. The previous reading showed inventories rising by 20B, indicating net injections into storage. The latest figure, however, reveals a 24B withdrawal, suggesting stronger consumption, reduced supply to storage, or a combination of both. Such a turnaround can reflect changing weather patterns, power generation needs, or broader shifts in energy usage. Market participants will be watching subsequent reports closely to see whether this draw signals the start of a sustained tightening trend in U.S. natural gas fundamentals or a short-term fluctuation in storage dynamics.
